data.exact_reserve_text: The claims development table shows the Syndicate's cumulative incurred claims development, including both claims notified and incurred but not reported for each underwriting year, together with the cumulative payments to date on a gross and net of reinsurance basis at the balance sheet date.
data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a gross prior year strengthening of USD 21.711 million, calculated from the claims development triangle. This strengthening is primarily due to adverse development on the 2015 underwriting year, partially offset by a release on the 2014 underwriting year. The report also notes a net increase in incurred claims relating to 2016 and prior years of USD 50.3 million. Causes for reserve movements include unforeseen loss trends, court rulings, changes in law, differences in loss adjustment practice, medical and long-term care, and economic factors such as inflation. No specific named events were quantified as impacting prior year reserves.
raw_causal_phrases: Unforeseen loss trends resulting from court rulings, changes in the law, differences in loss adjustment practice, medical and long-term care, and economic factors such as inflation can have a considerable impact on run-off results.

The uncertainty associated with the ultimate claims experience of an underwriting year is greatest when the underwriting year is at an early stage of development and the margin for future experience potentially being more adverse than assumed is at its highest.
initial reserves may not always be sufficient.
